channel.title: NotchPop
channel.description: Updates for NotchPop — your MacBook notch, but useful.

item.title: v1.5.6
item.description:
v1.5.6 — Timer end-sound (with picker + preview)

  • Bug fix: the existing 'Sound effects' toggle wasn't actually wired to the timers — both Pomodoro and Countdown were unconditionally calling NSSound.beep() regardless of the setting. Now they go through a shared TimerSound helper that honors the toggle.
  • Sound picker in Settings → Pomodoro: choose between Beep (the system alert sound) and 11 of macOS's built-in named sounds — Glass, Submarine, Bell, Hero, Funk, Frog, Pop, Sosumi, Tink, Ping, Purr. Default is Glass (same chime macOS uses for Calendar alerts).
  • Preview button next to the picker — clicking it always plays the chosen sound, even if the master toggle is off, so you can audition before committing.
  • The single setting applies to both Pomodoro phase ends and the Countdown timer.
  • Cleaned up Settings: the old 'Sound effects' toggle in Behavior was redundant; removed it with a pointer to Pomodoro pane instead.

item.title: v1.5.5
item.description:
v1.5.5 — Centered notch + tighter hover + timer live preview + advancing progress bar

  • Notch is now actually centered over the hardware notch. applyContentSize was using window.frame.midX which drifts as the window resizes asymmetrically. Switched to screen.frame.midX so the visible shape is locked to the screen center, regardless of how wide the live activity makes it.
  • Hover is much less twitchy. The 18pt invisible hover gutter beneath the notch was triggering accidentally any time you moved past the top of the screen. Cut to 4pt — your mouse now has to actually be on the notch shape to open it.
  • Timer live preview now actually appears. The Pomodoro / Countdown live activity wasn't re-rendering when the timer started. Fixed by adding objectWillChange.send() on the relevant Combine sinks (pomodoro.$running, countdown.$running) so SwiftUI knows to re-evaluate the live activity body.
  • Music progress bar now advances. Added a 1-second local elapsed-advance timer that bumps track.elapsed while playing. The 5-second AppleScript probe still re-syncs to the real value periodically.
  • Pomodoro remaining and Countdown remaining changes also force re-renders so the live preview's countdown text ticks every second.

item.title: v1.5.4
item.description:
v1.5.4 — NotchNook-style live activities + bug fixes

What changed

  • Live activity is now ONE integrated wide pill — matching the NotchNook reference design. The notch grows wider with the icon on the left and content on the right (animated audio bars for music, countdown text for timer). Single continuous black shape, not two flanking pills.
  • Music: now shows actual play state — case-insensitive parsing of 'Playing' / 'Paused' / 'Stopped' so macOS 26's variant codes don't slip through as 'paused'. Optimistic state flip when you click the play button so the icon updates instantly.
  • Music: artwork loads via three paths — raw AppleScript data, then 'data of artwork 1', then a fallback that queries iTunes Search API for the cover (works without Apple Events permission).
  • Settings opens reliably — switched from NSApp.responds(to:) probing to NSApp.sendAction which goes through the responder chain SwiftUI's Settings scene actually listens to.
  • Settings gear in the notch — small ⚙ button next to the battery indicator in the expanded view. One click opens Settings.
  • Version label in the notch — small v1.5.4 tag in the top-right of the expanded view so you always know what you're on.
  • Drag-to-shelf forces Shelf visible — even if you've hidden the Shelf tab, dragging a file in temporarily adds it back so you have a real drop target.

Note

If music isn't detected, check System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation → NotchPop and make sure Music + Spotify are checked. macOS only prompts once and silent-denies forever after.

item.title: v1.5.3
item.description:
v1.5.3 — Drag-to-shelf is way easier now

  • Drop zone is now the entire window, not just the visible notch shape. You no longer have to aim at a 178pt sliver — anywhere near the top of the screen counts.
  • Auto-expand on drag-hover — the moment you start dragging a file toward the notch, it expands to the full Shelf view. Big drop target waiting for you instead of a tiny pill.
  • Visible drop ring — pink → blue gradient stroke appears around the notch while you're dragging so you know it's targeted.
  • Drag leaves the window without dropping → notch collapses back after a brief grace period.

item.title: v1.5.2
item.description:
v1.5.2 — Live activities

  • 🎵 Music pill — when something is playing in Apple Music or Spotify, a slim pill appears just to the right of the collapsed notch with album art + scrolling track title. Tap to open the Music tab.
  • ⏱ Timer pill — when Pomodoro or Countdown is running, the time-remaining pill sits to the left of the notch. Pomodoro takes priority and shows the phase emoji + a tiny progress arc. Tap to open the Pomodoro/Timers tab.
  • Toggle the whole feature in Settings → Behavior → Live activities.
  • This is the first auto-updated release — if you're on v1.5.1 you should see this install itself within ~4 hours, with system notifications.

item.title: v1.5.1
item.description:
v1.5.1 — Auto-update + bug fixes

  • 🚀 Auto-update via Sparkle — NotchPop checks for updates every 4 hours, signs them with EdDSA, and posts a system notification when an update is found / installed.
  • 🎵 Music probe fix — added NSAppleEventsUsageDescription so macOS Sequoia stops silently blocking AppleScript reads of Music/Spotify track info. Plus a 5-second re-probe covers songs that started after launch.
  • 📋 Clipboard widget · 🖥 System Stats widget · proper app icon · all carryover from v1.5.0.
